q: The herbicide DCMU blocks electron flow from PSII to plastoquinone. What happens to O2 release by illuminated chloroplasts?
options: It stops: PSII can't pass on electrons, so P680+ isn't regenerated to split water
It increases, because electrons trapped in PSII are diverted into splitting extra water
It continues normally, but production of NADPH by PSI increases to compensate
It continues, but the O2 is now released from CO2 instead of from water
explanation: With the path out of PSII blocked, its primary acceptor stays reduced, so P680 can't keep emitting electrons. No new P680+ forms, so there is no oxidising power to split water – O2 release stops, and so does non-cyclic production of ATP and NADPH. This shows photolysis depends on continuous electron flow away from PSII.
